mobile_390.note: Headings scale up well; body text stays around 14 px with generous line height.

desktop_1440.note: Peach, white and dark-brown bands alternate, separated by wavy or scalloped edges; small hand-drawn baker characters and sparkle marks recur at section openings.

mobile_390.note: The same bands and wave edges, one column, with the characters kept at small size.

desktop_1440.note: No booking or order action; orange pill buttons lead to more pages, and each store has a map button.

mobile_390.note: The phone numbers are tap-to-call links in the shop details; there is no fixed action bar.

desktop_1440.note: Two stores, each with address, phone, hours and closing days written as text beside a store photo.

mobile_390.note: The same store details stack under a store photo and stay readable at phone width.

desktop_1440.note: Under the hero, a row of five small icon links with English and Japanese labels; a fixed header with the same links appears while scrolling.

mobile_390.note: A round orange menu button fixed at the top right.

desktop_1440.note: Warm, close food photography plus store interiors, an Instagram grid and simple line characters; colours limited to peach, orange and dark brown.

mobile_390.note: Same photography; round and blob-shaped photo crops keep a soft feel.

design_features: Wavy and scalloped section edges and a recurring baker character give the shop a friendly, local identity.
Three numbered commitments with large orange numerals and round photos explain why the bread is special.
Each store has a complete text block with address, phone, hours and closing days.

transferable_techniques.technique: Numbered commitments with large numerals and one photo each
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: Visitors read the shop's reasons in a fixed order, and the numerals make the list easy to scan.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Shops with two to four real, specific commitments stated by the owner.
transferable_techniques.risk: With vague or invented claims it becomes generic marketing; more than four dilutes it.

transferable_techniques.technique: Complete text shop details per location
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: Hours, closing days and phone are readable and copyable, not hidden in images.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Any shop; essential for multi-store or irregular hours.
transferable_techniques.risk: Low risk; only the layout must stay plain enough to read on a phone.

weaknesses: Desktop body text is small for the width, and the story band's white text sits over a busy photo.
A banner about a media appearance interrupts the flow near the news.
No direct way to order or reserve, which suits walk-in only.
desktop_vs_mobile: Desktop shows an icon link row under the hero; the phone hides it behind a round menu button.
Numbered commitments sit beside their photos on desktop and stack photo-first on the phone.
do_not_transfer: Its logo, characters, photographs and wording.
Its exact wave shapes, palette values and section order.

desktop_1440.note: Centred round house-shaped logo with a lowercase wordmark, a centred one-line nav, then a three-slide photo carousel held inside the content width rather than full bleed. The first screen showed a kitchen lunch photo; the full-page capture showed cookies, so the opening image changes.

mobile_390.note: Logo centred with a MENU button at the right, the same carousel cropped to a wide strip, then a large vertical-set (tategaki) statement in two columns before any body text.

desktop_1440.note: The signature cookie is named in the intro paragraph; a lineup band shows three product cards (photo, name, one or two lines of description) in a row with one shared see-more button.

mobile_390.note: The three product cards stack in one column with the same name and description; in this capture their photos had not loaded, leaving tall empty boxes.

desktop_1440.note: Rounded Gothic throughout; section titles pair a Japanese heading with a small italic English subtitle. Body text is small for a 1440 screen and set in a narrow centred column.

mobile_390.note: Body text is comfortable at phone width with generous line height; the vertical statement is the largest type on the page and only appears in the mobile capture.

desktop_1440.note: Sections alternate between a cream ground and a beige band with no rules or borders; each section ends with the same small dark-brown button, giving a steady beat.

mobile_390.note: The same cream and beige alternation, with long gaps where lazy images did not render in this capture; the online-store photo moves above its text.

desktop_1440.note: No single main action. Each section has a small dark-brown see-more button; the online store button carries an outbound-link icon.

mobile_390.note: The same buttons become wider centred pills; still no fixed or repeated main action such as a call or visit button.

desktop_1440.note: Café days and hours sit inside the kitchen section; the footer area lists postcode, address, phone, shop hours and the closing day in small type above a dark-brown footer.

mobile_390.note: The same address block appears near the end, readable but only after a long scroll; café hours and shop hours are given in two different places.

desktop_1440.note: Eight centred text links, two with dropdown markers; the footer repeats the links in two short columns.

mobile_390.note: A MENU button replaces the links; the dark-brown footer lists all links centred one per line.

desktop_1440.note: Warm natural-light food photography of the baked goods, gift boxes and the café lunch; colours limited to cream, beige and dark brown so the photos carry the warmth.

mobile_390.note: The same photography, cropped to wide strips; social icons are dark-brown circles that match the buttons.

design_features: A three-colour system of cream ground, beige bands and dark brown for logo, buttons and footer, with no other accent colour except a red notice line.
Section headings pair Japanese with a small italic English subtitle, so every section reads the same way.
On a phone, a large vertical-set statement sits between the hero and the body text as a pause.

transferable_techniques.technique: Two alternating ground tones instead of rules between sections
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: Sections separate clearly while the page stays calm and warm; no borders compete with the photos.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Small food or craft shops with warm photography and a limited palette.
transferable_techniques.risk: With weak photos the page becomes flat beige blocks; the tones need enough contrast to read as separate bands.

transferable_techniques.technique: Vertical-set statement as a pause after the hero on mobile
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: It gives one sentence of brand voice its own screen and slows the scroll before the details.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Japanese shops whose own wording supplies a short statement. Second Root's vertical_name allows only the shop name to be vertical, so a vertical statement would need a separate approval.
transferable_techniques.risk: Takes a full screen on a phone; with long or invented text it delays the practical information.

transferable_techniques.technique: Product trio cards with name and one-line description
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: Visitors see what the shop sells and its signature item without leaving the top page.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Shops with three or so clearly named products backed by real facts.
transferable_techniques.risk: Needs approved product images; forcing exactly three equal cards hides a signature item that deserves a bigger slot, and stock images look worse than a text list.

weaknesses: The opening image rotates, so a first-time visitor may see the café lunch instead of the signature cookie.
On a 1440 screen the body text is small and the content column narrow, leaving wide empty margins.
Café hours and shop hours are in different sections, which can confuse a visitor checking when to come.
No visible main action such as call or visit; all buttons are equal see-more links.
desktop_vs_mobile: The vertical statement was visible only in the mobile capture; on desktop the intro starts directly with a small paragraph.
Desktop nav is a centred link row; on a phone it collapses into a MENU button.
The online-store block is side by side on desktop and stacks image-first on a phone.
do_not_transfer: Its logo, photographs, product names and wording.
Its exact palette values and its exact section order and layout.

second_opinion.summary: ChatGPT (from the PR records, not the screenshots): palette, spacing and consistent product cards are useful; section separation by ground colour suits small shops. Do not force three equal cards; a signature item may deserve a larger slot.

design_features: The gallery entry shows an older hero (a large English slogan) than the live site, so the gallery alone would have misled about the current design.
A brand-values index: five one-kanji words, each with a thin leader line to short sub-topics.
A store list grouped by brand, with a tiny region label above each Latin store name.
Action buttons pair an English label with a small Japanese label underneath.
On the phone capture the value rows ran past the right edge; whether that is a slide-in animation caught mid-way or a real overflow was not confirmed.

transferable_techniques.technique: Vertical-set announcement in a side column beside a large photo
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: The photo keeps full impact while a short message reads in its own quiet column.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Japanese shops with one strong approved image and one short factual announcement. Vertical text other than the shop name is outside the approved vertical_name scope and needs its own approval.
transferable_techniques.risk: Built for a multi-store brand; on a small single shop it can feel borrowed. Needs real text, and on a phone it must fall back to horizontal text.

transferable_techniques.technique: Small region label above each store or location name
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: A long list of places stays scannable because the location is read first and the name second.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Businesses with two or more locations.
transferable_techniques.risk: Pointless for a single-location shop; tiny grey labels can fall below readable contrast.

transferable_techniques.technique: Action buttons with a main label and a small plain-language sublabel
transferable_techniques.why_it_works: A stylish label stays while the sublabel says plainly what the button does.
transferable_techniques.where_it_fits: Shops with one or two real actions (booking, online shop).
transferable_techniques.risk: Three or more such buttons in one bar split attention; grey-on-grey buttons are low contrast.

weaknesses: The restaurant booking, cafe booking and online shop buttons compete; no single main action.
Light grey text and grey buttons on a pale grey ground give low contrast.
desktop_vs_mobile: Desktop places the header bar under the hero; on a phone it moves to the top above the hero.
The vertical announcement on desktop becomes horizontal text on a phone.
Desktop shows three action buttons, the phone header shows two.
do_not_transfer: Its slatted photo treatment, wordmark, photographs and wording.
Its exact layout, value words and store-list design as a whole.

second_opinion.summary: ChatGPT (from the PR records, not the screenshots): the split of roles between large photo and typography is useful, but a multi-store brand expression should not be moved onto a small single shop. Clipped rows and fade-in need checking after animations finish.
